name: Beatrice San Claire
source_profile:
Contessa Beatrice San Claire, House San Claire 
Beatrice is a dignified and politically astute noblewoman from an ancient southern house, 
respected for her education, diplomacy, and religious patronage. Unlike Godric Renshaw, she 
opposed the former king's restrictions on northern noble titles, arguing that they threatened the 
stability of the kingdom. Nevertheless, when the northern lords declared secession, she 
remained loyal to the crown. Her levies served with distinction during the civil war, although she 
repeatedly advocated negotiation and leniency toward defeated soldiers. Following the war, 
Beatrice emerged as a supporter of the young king's reconciliation efforts. She regards the 
creation of the eastern marquisates as an opportunity for reconstruction, but worries that the 
heavy tallage may encourage reckless expansion and exploitation. 
 

Political tension: Beatrice is respected throughout Cador but sometimes dismissed by hardline 
nobles as overly accommodating. She believes the kingdom can accommodate both its ancient 
southern traditions and the commercial institutions of the north.

The Duchy of Orleade 
The great political prize of the northern rebellion. 
Duke Severin Halewick, House Halewick 
Severin comes from a wealthy and politically influential northern family whose interests lie in 
banking, manufacturing, and naval commerce. His house was among the most important 
northern supporters of the crown during the civil war. The Halewicks acquired Orleade following 
the rebellion's defeat, making Severin one of the most powerful nobles in the kingdom almost 
overnight. He is a capable administrator, but his greatest challenge is legitimacy. Many of 
Orleade's oldest institutions still contain officials who served the previous duke. 
The Great Eastway 
The Great Eastway, officially the King's Highroad, is an ancient thoroughfare stretching from the 
western coast of Cador in the Duchy of Orleade, through the forests and farmlands of the north, 
and eastward to the kingdom's frontier. For centuries, it has served as one of Cador's principal 
arteries of commerce and travel, providing a vital overland route connecting the eastern reaches 
of the realm to Orleade, and the Royal Duchy of Cade by way of a southern spur route. Known 
to many as the Marchway, its well-traveled stretches gradually give way to rougher roads and 
lonely wilderness trails toward the eastern marches, where frontiersmen have fittingly dubbed it 
the Long Road.
